description: One-level and two-level directory_idle waits differ on the same writer: the first fires while the log two levels down is still growing, the second does not.
turns: The workspace {workspace} holds writer.cmd, which keeps appending to out\level1\build.log for about forty seconds. Launch it with cmd.exe and arguments ["/d","/c","writer.cmd"] using process_run, with waitTimeoutMs=100 so the call returns while the writer is still running. Then make two trigger_wait calls, in this order. First a single directory_idle condition on {workspace}/out with quietMs=1200 and timeoutMs=8000, without naming a depth. Then a single directory_idle condition on the same folder with quietMs=1200, depth=2 and timeoutMs=6000. Report what each wait returned, the outcome, the number of entries it counted and the depth it covered, and explain why the two differ. Keep writer.cmd and writer.ps1 unchanged.

checks.name: launches the writer and keeps the call short
one level fires with a single entry
two levels does not fire while the log grows
reports the depth of the count
reports the entry count of each wait
